results.title: Koyeb Review 2026: Pricing, GPU Costs and Fine Print After the Mistral Deal | The Proof Desk
results.author: The Proof Desk Team
highlights:
Koyeb has gone from a scrappy Heroku alternative with a free tier to a GPU-first serverless cloud that Mistral AI has agreed to buy. The pricing changed with it: the free Starter plan is gone for new users, the real entry point is the $29 Pro plan, and GPUs are cheaper than ever, with an H100 at $2.50 an hour.

...

### Koyeb at a glance (November 2026)

Plans: Pro $29/mo, Scale $299/mo, Enterprise from $1,000/mo, all plus compute. Cheapest CPU instance: eco-nano at $1.61/mo, standard nano at $2.68/mo. GPUs from $0.50/hr (RTX 4000 SFF Ada) to $5.50/hr (B200). Free tier for new users: none. Uptime SLA: 99.9% on Scale, 99.99% on Enterprise, none on Pro.

...

On February 17, 2026 Koyeb announced it had "entered into a definitive agreement to join Mistral AI", the Paris-based model maker. It is Mistral's first acquisition, the terms were not disclosed, and Koyeb's own post says completion "is subject to closing conditions". Trade press reported the roughly 16-person team joining Mistral in March 2026, but we found no official closing notice from Koyeb, so treat it as an agreed deal rather than a confirmed close.

...

Koyeb announced the definitive agreement on February 17, 2026; the pricing page now carries the same message.

...

Koyeb's public changelog has not had a new entry since February 27, 2026, ten days after the deal was announced. The platform keeps running, but public product updates have slowed noticeably.

...

Pro's $10 of included compute covers almost exactly one standard small instance (1 vCPU, 1GB) running all month at $10.71. Anything beyond that is billed on top of the $29 fee.

## Serverless GPUs: the strongest part of the offer

GPUs are where Koyeb is most competitive. In November 2025 it cut prices by up to 24%: L40S from $1.55 to $1.20/hr, A100 from $2.00 to $1.60/hr, and H100 from $3.30 to $2.50/hr. RTX Pro 6000, H200 and B200 arrived in January 2026. All GPU instances are billed by the second.

- RTX 4000 SFF Ada (20GB): $0.50/hr
- L4 (24GB): $0.70/hr
- RTX A6000 (48GB): $0.75/hr
- L40S (48GB): $1.20/hr
- A100 (80GB): $1.60/hr
- A100 SXM (80GB): $2.15/hr
- RTX Pro 6000 (96GB): $2.20/hr
- H100 (80GB): $2.50/hr
- H200 (141GB): $3.00/hr
- B200 (180GB): $5.50/hr

Multi-GPU configurations scale linearly: 2x, 4x and 8x A100 at $3.20, $6.40 and $12.80/hr; 2x, 4x and 8x H100 at $5.00, $10.00 and $20.00/hr; 2x, 4x and 8x H200 at $6.00, $12.00 and $24.00/hr. Tenstorrent N300s cards are listed as request access.

### Listed is not the same as available

In the pricing page catalog, L4, B200, 4x H200 and every 8x configuration are marked restricted with no self-serve region. Expect to contact sales before you can deploy them. The status page also logged "RTXA6000 currently unavailable" on September 15, 2026, so capacity on popular cards can run out.

...

### How much is an H100 on Koyeb?

$2.50 per hour for a single H100 80GB, billed by the second, down from $3.30 before the November 2025 price cut. 2x, 4x and 8x H100 configurations cost $5, $10 and $20 per hour, though 8x setups are marked restricted.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

...

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

results.title: Nebius moves spare GPU hours to spot prices | Wire
results.author: Sean
highlights:
Nebius switched its spare GPU hours from a fixed price to live spot pricing on 8 October. An H100 hour now floats between $0.79 and $4.49. Nebius gets paid more when clusters are full. The stuck step is the idle hour, and only the console shows it.

...

Nebius no longer sells its spare GPU hours at a fixed price. Since 8 October 2026, its interruptible (preemptible) GPU hours float. An H100 hour now costs anywhere from $0.79 to $4.49. Until last week it was a flat $2.15. The price moves with how full Nebius's clusters are, and it can change every 15 minutes. On the neocloud model, this is the idle-hour step: Nebius now gets paid more for spare chips when they are scarce, and less when they sit.

...

Nebius, the GPU cloud that rents Nvidia chips by the hour, updated its compute price list for October. Two changes, a week apart:

8 October

Preemptible B300, B200, H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000 hours move to dynamic spot pricing

Nebius Compute pricing documentation

The band

Floor of $0.79 (H100, H200) or $0.99 (B200, B300). Ceiling one cent below the on-demand rate

Price set by capacity, cluster use, customer demand and pricing preferences

1 October

On-demand rates up 17% to 21%: H100 $3.85 to $4.50, B300 $7.85 to $9.50

This raised the spot ceiling too, since the ceiling tracks on-demand

Who can see the price

Current and past spot prices sit inside the Nebius console, not on a public page

...

Sources: Nebius, Compute pricing in Nebius AI Cloud, read 9 Oct 2026: from 1 Oct 2026 on-demand H100 $4.50 (was $3.85), H200 $5.40 (was $4.50), B200 $8.50 (was $7.15), B300 $9.50 (was $7.85); from 8 Oct 2026 preemptible pricing for B300, B200, H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000 switches to dynamic spot pricing, preemptible from $0.79 (H100, H200, RTX PRO 6000) and from $0.99 (B200, B300), previously fixed at $2.15 (H100), $2.45 (H200), $3.95 (B200), $4.30 (B300) and $0.95 (RTX PRO 6000); spot prices can change as often as every 15 minutes and the highest is one cent below the on-demand rate; Nebius price page, read 9 Oct 2026: commitment discounts of up to 35% off on-demand for multi-month cluster reservations, current spot prices shown in the Nebius console; GPU Cloud Advisors, 28 Sep 2026: 1 Oct increase of 17% to 21%. The monthly server cost examples, the ceilings as a multiple of the old price, and the spread are our arithmetic. Not investment advice. Do your own research.

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

results.title: Nebius GPU prices rise across the board, up to… · Slicast
highlights:
# Nebius GPU prices rise across the board, up to 21%; H100 cumulative gain of 53% over five months

Trade press Slicast · October 1, 2026 at 21:01 UTC · Global · Source: KuCoin News

A notable shift is emerging in the AI computing power market: while cloud providers continue to expand their data centers, rental prices for certain high-end GPUs are not declining with increased supply—they continue to rise.

According to a price adjustment notice sent by Nebius to its customers, effective October 1, 2026, the company plans to increase prices for multiple on-demand GPU instances by approximately 17% to 21%. The proposed hourly rates per GPU are: H100 rising from $3.85 to $4.50 (a 16.9% increase), H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (20% increase), B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 (18.9% increase), and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50 (21% increase).

This price adjustment sends a significant signal: the pace of growth in AI computing demand may still outstrip the rate at which high-end GPUs, power, and data center capacity are coming online. Unlike traditional cloud computing, the core scarce resources for AI cloud services extend beyond servers to include GPU availability, power access, liquid cooling systems, networking equipment, and data centers capable of supporting high-density racks. If any single component encounters a bottleneck, new computing power cannot be rapidly deployed.

At the Goldman Sachs Technology Conference, Nebius management stated that the company's visibility into customer demand has extended from approximately 18 months to over 24 months, with some customers already reserving compute capacity for the first half of 2028. The company previously conducted price testing for scarce Blackwell capacity, achieving transaction prices approximately 15% higher than previous peak prices and roughly 20% higher than standard sales pipeline quotes.

The significance of Nebius's price increase lies not merely in the ability to charge approximately 20% more per GPU hour, but in confirming that supply and demand in the AI computing market still favor suppliers. A primary past market concern was that simultaneous launches of numerous data centers could eventually lead to GPU leasing market oversupply, potentially resulting in lower utilization rates, extended payback periods, and asset impairment for companies built under assumptions of higher prices. Nebius signals the opposite: the company is raising prices not only for new B200 and B300 models but also for H100 and H200, which have been on the market for years. This indicates that demand extends beyond the latest architecture, with previous-generation GPUs still offering sufficient performance and cost efficiency for model fine-tuning, inference, scientific computing, and certain enterprise workloads.

However, the on-demand price increase will not uniformly raise all of Nebius's revenue by 20%. Large customers typically sign multi-year contracts with fixed prices, minimum purchase volumes, and service terms that cannot be immediately repriced according to new public rates. This adjustment most directly impacts on-demand and short-term compute contracts rather than long-term capacity agreements already signed by clients like Meta.
